meta.title: Campfire
meta.tagline: Pull up a log. Plan tomorrow's ride.
meta.description: An unofficial, searchable companion to Red Dead Redemption 2: The Complete Official Guide (Piggyback, 2018). Facts and summaries are written in our own words; every topic points to the guide page it came from.
meta.source: Red Dead Redemption 2: The Complete Official Guide (Piggyback Interactive, 2018)
meta.disclaimer: Fan-made companion. Not affiliated with Rockstar Games, Take-Two Interactive or Piggyback. Base map artwork by Jotrius (J10 Railroad Engineer), used with permission. Pin positions come from the guide's atlas and are approximate where marked.

topics.title: On-screen display
topics.text:
What each part of the screen tells you.
- Reticle: appears when a weapon is drawn and turns red over a valid target. Headshots are the most efficient.
- Ammunition: the first number is shots left in the current weapon, the second is your total stock; the icon shows the ammo type selected.
- Attribute meters (lower left), left to right: health, stamina, Dead Eye, horse stamina, horse health.
- Radar: the mini-map with cardinal directions, objectives and points of interest. Hold the radar button to expand it or switch to a simple compass.
- Dynamic information: pop-up notices for items, rewards, objectives and wanted status.
- Context prompts: appear in the lower right whenever an action is possible; press, tap or hold the shown button.

topics.title: Essential commands
topics.text:
A recap of the core controls; most interactions are context prompts shown in the lower right.
- Movement: walk with the left stick; hold to run (no stamina cost, keeps your horse's pace after a gallop and follows companions); tap repeatedly to sprint (costs stamina). On horseback, tapping in rhythm with the gallop keeps top speed without draining horse stamina.
- Crouch-walk for stealth and hunting; you can also crouch-run.
- Aim and shoot: hold aim, line up, fire. Default aim assist locks onto the chest; a quick flick up as you lock on gives fast headshots.
- Shoot from the hip: fire without aiming to auto-target the nearest enemy.
- Dead Eye: slows time while aiming; once upgraded early in the story you can tag several targets and fire at all of them. It drains the Dead Eye meter.
- Cover: take/leave cover, slide along it, and pop out to fire.
- Reload manually during lulls, ideally from cover, to avoid an empty gun at the worst moment.
- Combat dive to dodge charges; silent takedown from behind (non-lethal unarmed, lethal with a knife); melee with block, counter and grapple.
- Holster your weapon when it isn't needed; walking around armed can cause trouble.

topics.title: Exploration commands and control tables
topics.text:
- Eagle Eye: highlights nearby tracks and collectibles; focus on a track to keep it visible after leaving Eagle Eye.
- Jump, vault and climb with the same button.
- Hold to open your satchel (or your horse's cargo when next to it) to heal, use items, read documents and check collectibles.
- Other general controls: tap for the log, hold for the Journal; whistle; hold to talk to nearby people; toggle camera views (hold for cinematic camera); hold the pause button to jump straight to the map.
- Horse controls: pat, gallop, follow a companion and match speed, jump, mount/dismount, hitch, lead, kick to the side, check stored weapons, brush, feed, check cargo, call your horse.
- Combat controls: peek from cover, dive, block, grapple, Dead Eye, weapon wheel, warning shot into the sky, toggle shoulder view.
- Map controls: place/remove markers and a waypoint, zoom, show the map index.

topics.title: Game structure, missions and saving
topics.text:
- Missions show on the map as a circle with the initials of the person you need to see. Talk to them there to start.
- The story is split into chapters; missions unlock as you meet conditions (the Missions chapter has the full unlock flowcharts).
- Every mission awards a medal based on how many of its medal goals you meet. Goals are only revealed in the Progress Story menu after you finish the mission once, so it's fine to ignore them on a first playthrough.
- Replay any story mission from Progress Story in the pause menu.
- Saving: the game autosaves at story milestones, after notable feats, and when you sleep at camp or in a bed. You can also save manually from the Story option in the pause menu, except during missions and some activities.

topics.title: Free roaming, difficulty and accessibility
topics.text:
- Outside missions you can roam freely; you'll keep running into collectibles, gangs, lawmen, fishing spots, ambushes and random events. Pick up optional activities when they're on your route, since travel time is the real cost.
- There are no difficulty modes, but several options help:
- Toggle View cycles four camera distances; the farthest makes it easier to track enemies and spot collectibles, first person is more immersive but harder.
- Lock-On Mode (Settings > Controls): choose how strongly aim snaps to targets, separately on foot and on horseback. Wide assist makes fights much easier; Free Aim removes all assistance.
- Tap Assist: fewer button presses, or hold instead of tapping, in mash sequences.
- Skip Checkpoint: fail a section three times in a row and you can skip ahead, usually about a minute of play.

topics.title: Traveling efficiently and fast travel
topics.text:
- When riding toward a place you've already visited, a recommended route is drawn on the map; it's reliable but not always the fastest. Reading the map yourself helps you find shortcuts.
- The map is topographic: contour lines show elevation. Flat plains let you ride straight at the target; mountains and canyons force winding paths.
- Fast Travel: a camp upgrade adds a map near your bed that lets you jump to key places you've visited, mainly towns and a few landmarks.
- Trains and stagecoaches, unlocked by early story missions, take you almost instantly to towns you've visited; the fare depends on distance.

topics.title: Map, radar and markers
topics.text:
- Open the map from the pause menu, or hold the pause button to go straight to it. Your position is a pin pointing the way you face. Scroll, zoom, place one waypoint (draws a route) and any number of markers; press the index button for a full icon list.
- The map starts hidden and is revealed as you explore, with labels added when you discover places and animal habitats.
- Radar: a small view of the map around you. Enemies are red dots; off-radar threats show as a red edge indicator. Search zones are shaded yellow or white. Mission blips, your horse, waypoints and markers stay visible at the radar's edge even when far away.
- Map legend icons include enemy, corpse, mission vendor, stranger, campsite, gang camp, barber, butcher, doctor, general store, gunsmith, hotel, newspaper seller, post office, saloon, show, stable, stagecoach, train station, tailor, trapper, bait shop, and the table games (Five Finger Fillet, poker, blackjack, dominoes).

topics.title: Locations: camp, towns and icon states
topics.text:
- Grayed-out service icons mean unavailable: closed (come back during opening hours), locked (opens later in the story), or shut because you're wanted. A small inset icon means something new is waiting there.
- Camp: gang members marked with their initials have missions for you. They also have lots of ambient conversations and scenes.
- After an early mission for Leopold Strauss, the ledger outside Dutch's tent lets you buy camp upgrades (for example Fast Travel or better free supplies). Fund them by donating to the tithing box beside it.
- Camp services: your tent (sleep, shave, change clothes); Pearson the cook and butcher (donate hunting spoils, and he crafts upgrades such as bigger satchels); provisions at Pearson's wagon; ammo and arms at Arthur's wagon; health supplies at Strauss's wagon; camp stew; chores; your personal savings.

topics.title: Town services, the wilderness and the day/night cycle
topics.text:
Town services:
- Barber: haircuts and shaves; changing your look can help you avoid recognition while wanted.
- Butcher: buys and sells animal parts. Doctor: tonics and stimulants for you and your horse. General store: provisions, hunting and fishing gear, clothing. Gunsmith: weapons and ammo.
- Fence: illegal goods such as dynamite and moonshine, plus rare items like talismans and trinkets.
- Hotel: sleep, bathe (cleans you and restores cores) and change clothes. Photo studio: portraits. Newspaper seller: news.
- Post office (often at the station): send and receive mail, and pay off bounties.
- Saloon: drinks and meals. Shows: entertainment for a small fee. Stable: buy, sell, customize and equip horses. Train stations and stagecoaches: travel between regions. Tailor and trapper: clothing. Table games: Five Finger Fillet, poker, blackjack and dominoes.
The wilderness:
- Animals have their own habitats; rivers and lakes hold fish (you get a rod in Chapter 2).
- You can make camp almost anywhere outside towns from the item wheel to sleep, craft and cook.
- Regions have different climates; wear the right outfit or heat and cold will drain your cores.
- One in-game day lasts 48 real minutes (time passes more slowly at camp). Some shops, characters, missions and animals depend on the hour; sleep at a campfire, your tent or a rented room to skip ahead (you get three duration options).

topics.title: Attributes, meters and cores
topics.text:
- Five attributes: health, stamina and Dead Eye for you; stamina and health for your horse.
- Each has a circular main meter and an inner core. The main meter drains with damage or effort and refills from tonics, sleep, and the core's regeneration (over time for health and stamina, with each kill for Dead Eye).
- Your meters grow as you earn attribute experience from related actions, gaining extra segments at milestones.
- Cores act as a last reserve: once the main meter is empty, more damage or effort drains the core. Emptying the health meter and its core means death.
- Core level controls how fast the main meter refills, so keeping cores full matters in fights.
- Cores empty in about 90 minutes under normal conditions, faster in harsh weather.
- Refill cores by sleeping, bathing or eating. You can preview an item's effect before using it.
- Sleep options: a campfire anywhere outside towns (available after the mission "Exit Pursued by a Bruised Ego"), your bed at the gang camp, or a rented room in town.
- More on cores and attribute training: page 167.

topics.title: Quick ways to level health, stamina and Dead Eye
topics.text:
- Health: land melee knockouts or thrown-weapon kills; rowing a boat also works well. Keep tonics for emergencies.
- Stamina: sprinting drains it most. Alternate sprinting and running so the meter refills without eating into the core. Sprint often and for long stretches to level it.
- Horse stamina: tap the gallop button in time with your horse's stride to ride at full speed without draining it.
- Dead Eye: activate it while aiming. After the early upgrade you can tag targets, including the same target several times, then fire. Level it with long-range headshots and free-aim kills.
- Full list of training methods: page 167.

topics.title: Horses: care, bonding, saddling and stables
topics.text:
- Keep your horse fed and clean; hunger and dirt drag down its health and stamina cores. Oatcakes, apples and hay fill it more than treats and also build bonding; some wild herbs work too. Overfeeding makes it gain weight (page 135).
- New horses without a stable: break a wild horse (lasso it if needed, calm it, mount it, and lean against its bucking until it's tamed), or steal one (not from gang members). These are only temporary.
- A horse becomes truly yours when you put your saddle on it (unlocked a few hours into the story). You have one saddle, so one main horse at a time.
- Higher bonding gives more health and stamina, new commands, a longer and faster whistle response, the ability to cross deeper water and rough terrain, and less fleeing from predators.
- Bond by calming, patting, feeding when hungry, brushing when dirty, removing heavy cargo, leading, riding, swimming together, and hitching at posts or trees (a hitched horse regains cores faster and won't wander).
- Gunshots can spook a new horse; use silent weapons like the bow until bonding raises its courage.
- Whistle range starts short. Your horse won't come if it's too far, stabled, or you're indoors or at camp.
- Stables: buy and sell horses, buy care items, buy or upgrade saddles, saddlebags and stirrups, keep up to three horses, and customize or rename them.

topics.title: Crime: robberies, loansharking, bounty hunting and fences
topics.text:
- Robberies unlock after the first few missions: shops, homesteads, camps, and later stagecoaches and trains (post office clerks sometimes tip you off about targets). Draw your weapon inside to intimidate; deal with would-be heroes quickly and get away without a long chase.
- Loansharking: Leopold Strauss sends you to make debtors pay up; debtors show as a dollar icon on the map.
- Bounty hunting: take posters from noticeboards at depots or sheriff's offices, then bring targets to the sheriff. Bringing them in alive (lasso, hogtie, carry on your horse) earns more honor than killing them. Scout their hideouts first.
- Fences buy stolen goods without questions. Two specialist fences, one for stolen wagons and one for stolen horses, unlock in the early chapters.
- Honor: good deeds (rescuing people, turning in criminals) raise it; killing innocents and stealing lower it. Reaching ranks unlocks benefits; full details on page 170.

topics.title: Witnesses and the wanted system
topics.text:
- Witnesses run to report crimes. Stop them (focus and use the interaction) or tackle them, then talk them out of it. Act fast.
- Bodies that are found also bring lawmen to investigate; carry corpses somewhere hidden if needed.
- Once seen committing a crime, the law notes your description. Lower your recognizability by changing clothes, changing hair or beard (camp tent or barber), or wearing a mask or bandana.
- When wanted, the search area is a red circle on the map. Escaping is usually best: whistle for your horse and gallop out of the circle, then keep riding until the search ends. Hiding works too. Killing the lawmen raises your bounty sharply and brings tougher reinforcements.
- Each state tracks its own bounty, which grows with every crime. Murder, jailbreaks and robberies carry the highest bounties.
- After serious crimes expect posses, marshals and bounty hunters to ambush you on the road.
- Pay off a bounty at any post office to reset that state. More detail on page 174.

topics.title: Fighting with the gang, and rival gangs
topics.text:
- Gang members fight alongside you in many missions, but your own shooting decides most battles.
- If a companion who's essential to the mission dies, you restart from the last checkpoint, so protect them.
- Many rival gangs hold their own territory. Raiding their camps is dangerous but can pay off with good loot.

topics.title: Challenges (overview)
topics.text:
- Nine categories of ten challenges each, done in order: Bandit (theft and robbery), Explorer (treasure hunting), Gambler (table games), Herbalist (crafting and picking herbs), Master Hunter (hunting and skinning), Horseman (riding feats), Sharpshooter (shooting feats), Survivalist (crafting and fishing), Weapons Expert (knife and thrown-weapon feats).
- Finishing all ten in a category gives attribute boosts, cash and, best of all, reinforced equipment you can then buy at any trapper.
- Some come naturally from playing; the later ones take real effort. Full list and rewards: page 172.

topics.title: Hunting basics
topics.text:
- Track with Eagle Eye: animal trails glow, and focusing on one keeps it highlighted. You'll also see your scent drifting on the wind; approach from downwind. Footprints, droppings and remains of prey are clues too.
- Each species has its own habitat (maps on page 149).
- Weapon choice matters: damaged carcasses are worth less. Early on the bow is best, giving clean, quiet kills. Aim for the head or neck, and call the animal just before releasing so it lifts its head.
- Small game arrows give better pelts from small animals; poison arrows drop big animals quickly.
- Bait attracts animals (predators and herbivores need different types). Drop it, hide and wait a few minutes. Fresh carcasses also lure some carnivores. Cover scents hide your presence.
- After skinning, small parts go in your satchel and large ones on your horse. Cook meat at a campfire, donate parts to camp, or sell them to butchers, general stores and the trapper before they rot. Pearson uses some for satchel upgrades. Teeth and claws can become talismans (page 313).
- Skinning counts toward Master Hunter challenges.

topics.title: Fishing basics
topics.text:
- Equip the rod from the item wheel and pick bait suited to your target species.
- Keep the fish to eat or sell, or release it alive for honor. Small fish go in the satchel, large ones on your horse.
- Controls: hold to grip the rod, hold and release to cast, strike when the bobber is pulled under, then pull the rod against the fish's direction to tire it and reel in whenever it eases off.
- Species bite differently: some nibble first, some bite firmly again and again, predators strike without warning.
- Bait (bread, worms) is cheap but lost on every bite. Lures cost more but are reusable; reel them slowly so they look alive. There are lures for river, lake and swamp fish, and only lures attract large fish.
- Fish are harder to tempt in bad weather.
- Large and rare fish need special lures, sold notably at the Bait and Tackle shop in the bayou.
- Legendary fish spots: page 164. Full fishing chapter: page 163.

topics.title: Item and weapon types
topics.text:
Items:
- Provisions: eat, drink or smoke to refill cores (sometimes at another core's expense).
- Tonics: restore a main meter and usually add the Fortified effect, which temporarily extends that meter.
- Ingredients (cooking), materials (crafting), kit items (tools like binoculars or the bandana), valuables (sell or craft), documents (letters, maps, pamphlets), horse cargo (bodies and pelts on your horse).
Weapons:
- Pistols: weaker than revolvers but hold more and reload quickly. Revolvers: six shots, more damage and accuracy, slower reload.
- Rifles: accurate and powerful but slow-firing. Repeaters: faster fire and more capacity, less accuracy and damage. Sniper rifles: long-range damage and precision.
- Shotguns: close quarters only, great for rooms and chokepoints; slugs hit even harder.
- Bow: silent and accurate, with craftable special arrows. Melee: fists, knives, hatchets, swords. Throwables: throwing knives and tomahawks for quiet kills, fire bottles and dynamite for groups.
- Lasso: rope animals or people. Keep aiming, walk up and hogtie them; then you can loot, carry or load them on your horse. Untied targets break free quickly, and hogtied ones eventually escape if left alone.
- Maintenance: worn guns lose stats. Select a weapon in the wheel to inspect it and clean it with gun oil (from gunsmiths or looted), or pay a gunsmith to clean it.

topics.title: Ammunition, loadout, crafting, outfits and upgrades
topics.text:
- Special ammo: high velocity (range and penetration), split point (more impact damage), express and explosive (maximum damage), small game arrows (better small pelts), poison arrows (big animals), fire and dynamite arrows (area damage). Switch type in the weapon wheel.
- Get ammo by looting enemies, finding it, buying it from gunsmiths and general stores, or crafting it.
- Loadout: you carry a limited number of weapons. Stand by your horse's saddle and hold the wheel button to swap guns before missions (shotgun for crowds, bow for stealth, sniper rifle for distance).
- The wheel and satchel slow time but don't stop it; enemies keep shooting.
- Crafting: a few items on the go, many more at camp or a campfire. Some shops craft upgrades if you bring the materials.
- Outfits: dress for the weather or cores drain fast. Change at camp, a rented room, a tailor, or by your horse. Wear a mask or bandana for crimes; some areas need the right outfit to avoid being recognized.
- Upgrades: gunsmiths sell capacity and wear-reduction upgrades; Pearson crafts bigger satchels from the right parts; challenges later unlock reinforced gear.

sections.title: Primer
sections.intro: The core systems you need from the first hour: the screen, controls, how the world is structured, travel, attributes, horses, crime, challenges, hunting, fishing and items.

topics.title: The story so far and main characters
topics.text:
After a failed robbery in Blackwater, the Van der Linde gang flees into the Grizzly Mountains and is caught by a late spring blizzard.
- Dutch van der Linde: the gang's charismatic leader, hostile to government control and devoted to personal freedom, slowly realizing that way of life is ending.
- Arthur Morgan: the protagonist and Dutch's right hand, taken in by Dutch as a boy and loyal ever since, though Blackwater has shaken him.
- Hosea Matthews: the oldest member and Dutch's oldest friend; clever, calm and more realistic about the gang's future.
- Javier Escuella: a former bounty hunter and Mexican revolutionary who fled Nuevo Paraiso and joined four years ago; fiercely loyal.
- Abigail Roberts: John's partner and Jack's mother, brought to the gang by Uncle five years ago.
- John Marston: Dutch's protégé since age 12, unsure of his priorities as a partner and father; badly hurt at Blackwater.
- Uncle: a work-shy drinker who always turns up when there's whiskey.
- Micah Bell: with the gang for about five months; vindictive, and always backs Dutch.
- Bill Williamson: a dishonorably discharged ex-cavalry soldier, hot-tempered and loyal to Dutch; joined five years ago.
- Pinkertons: a private detective agency hired by the government to hunt outlaws like the gang.

topics.title: How chapters and medal goals work
topics.text:
- Each chapter's missions unlock in a set order, sometimes with conditions (for example, one in-game hour after another mission).
- A few stranger missions are tied to the story and are covered with the main chapters because they're time-sensitive: miss them before certain story points and they're gone.
- Medal rules: gold for completing every optional goal, silver for at least half, bronze for fewer than half.
- Goals are hidden until your first completion. The guide recommends playing at your own pace first and going for medals on replays (Progress Story menu), ideally after finishing the story.
- Gold medals aren't needed for total completion.
- Earning 70 gold medals in any missions unlocks the "Gold Rush" trophy/achievement.

topics.title: Time-sensitive trophies and achievements
topics.text:
Some trophies can only be earned at certain points in the story:
- Friends with Benefits: do a companion activity in every camp. Each time the gang moves, do at least one (list on page 146).
- Errand Boy: complete five item requests for gang members. Most are available from Chapter 2 to Chapter 4 (list on page 145).
- Breaking and Entering: recover the stash from four homesteads. Two of the home robberies are time-sensitive (page 182).
- Give to the Poor: donate $250 to the tithing box before the end of Chapter 4.
- Lending a Hand: complete all the optional honor missions in the main story.

topics.title: Chapter 1: Colter (overview)
topics.text:
The gang shelters at Colter in the snowbound Grizzlies.
- Missions in order: Outlaws from the West, Enter Pursued by a Memory, Old Friends, The Aftermath of Genesis, Who the Hell is Leviticus Cornwall?, Eastward Bound.
- Gear and features unlocked along the way: Cattleman Revolver, hunting knife, lantern, sawed-off shotgun, bow, dynamite, lasso, Carbine Repeater, and the Master Hunter challenges (page 173).
- Crafting unlocks at the end of Chapter 1, but it's worth gathering herbs and parts from the start; surplus can be sold.

topics.title: Outlaws from the West
topics.text:
Chapter 1. Ride with Dutch through the snow to the Adler homestead, where O'Driscolls are holed up.
Gold medal goals:
- Take no damage during the shootout
- Loot six or more items from Adler Ranch
- Finish with at least 80% accuracy
Walkthrough:
- Hitch your horse, follow Dutch, and take cover in the shed when told. Equip your revolver and protect Dutch: one gunman appears upstairs and another from the outhouse on your left. Let the fleeing O'Driscoll go; killing him lowers honor.
- Search the house, including furniture and the upper floor, for loot. Eat provisions (e.g. baked beans) from your satchel to top up your health core.
- In the barn, win the fistfight, interrogate the man, and grab your weapon and hat. Calm the horse, lead it out, hitch it, then go into the cabin.
Tip: the hard goal is taking no damage. Stay in cover and pop out only to drop one target at a time.

topics.title: Enter, Pursued by a Memory
topics.text:
Chapter 1. Go with Javier to find John Marston in the mountains.
Gold medal goals:
- Finish with at least 80% accuracy
- Kill all the wolves without taking any damage
Walkthrough:
- Follow Javier. At your horse, open the weapon wheel and choose the sawed-off shotgun.
- Crouch when prompted, then walk up the hill after the cutscene.
- When wolves attack, focus one at a time, shoot as soon as the reticle goes red (head if you can), and dive sideways when they lunge.
- More wolves attack on the ride back; shoot them as they circle Javier and John.
Tip: drop at least one wolf at range as they run downhill. Staying near Javier helps because the wolves go for him first, but he can't take many bites.

topics.title: Old Friends
topics.text:
Chapter 1. Start at the Colter camp marker and follow Dutch to raid an O'Driscoll camp.
Gold medal goals:
- Get 15 headshots
- Catch and hogtie Kieran in under 45 seconds
- Complete the mission in under 15 minutes 30 seconds
- Kill three O'Driscolls in the same Dead Eye use
- Complete the mission without using any health items
Walkthrough:
- Take the repeater from your horse when told; the guide suggests the Carbine Repeater and Cattleman Revolver.
- Choose to take the lead when Dutch asks, so you can open with a clean headshot.
- Move cover to cover and reload when safe. Watch for gunmen on high points such as the water tower.
- The second wave from the forest introduces Dead Eye: tag heads, then fire. Choose to defend when Dutch asks, for better cover, and keep your allies alive.
- Loot bodies and the camp, and get the dynamite from the large red crate in the yellow search area.
- On the ride back, chase the fleeing O'Driscoll (Kieran), lasso him, keep aiming as he falls, hogtie him, and carry him back to camp.
Tip: for the Dead Eye goal, tag three heads before firing.

topics.title: The Aftermath of Genesis
topics.text:
Chapter 1. Greet Pearson at camp to start, then go hunting with Charles.
Gold medal goals:
- Kill each deer with one arrow
- Do not spook either deer
- Get a clean kill on the second deer
Walkthrough:
- Take your bow from the saddle. Crouch-walk along the deer tracks in front of Charles; use Eagle Eye if you lose them.
- Draw the bow fully (listen for the string) but release before your stamina runs out. Hit the head or neck for a perfect pelt.
- The second deer is across the river; track it the same way.
- Pick up a carcass, whistle your horse (short range at first) and stow it. Back at camp, drop it in Pearson's kitchen and skin it.
Tip: crouch the whole time, stay out of sight and make each shot a headshot.

topics.title: Who the Hell is Leviticus Cornwall?
topics.text:
Chapter 1. Rob Leviticus Cornwall's train.
Gold medal goals:
- Save Lenny when he is hanging from the train
- After stopping the train, take out the guards within 1 minute 30 seconds
- Take no damage during the shootout
- Get ten headshots
- Complete the mission without using any health items
Walkthrough:
- Meet Bill at the water tower, pick up the spool and wire it to the detonator, then ride back up to Dutch above the tunnel.
- Choose your loadout first (Cattleman Revolver and Carbine Repeater suggested) and put on your bandana from the item wheel.
- Jump onto the train from the overhang, grab Lenny and mash to pull him up.
- Work toward the front, taking out guards (Lenny can take one; a silent takedown or headshot works). Mash to break free when grabbed, then pull the brake in the engine.
- When the train stops, take cover behind the nearby rock and pick off both waves.
- Blow the carriage door with dynamite from Bill, search the carriage, and open the lock box in the cabinet at the back for the bonds. Deal with the guards however you like, loot freely, then start the train to finish.
Tip: stay in cover during the shootout and take quick headshots when nobody is shooting at you.

topics.title: Eastward Bound
topics.text:
Chapter 1. The gang leaves the mountains for Horseshoe Overlook.
Gold medal goals:
- Pick up Javier when you enter Horseshoe Overlook
- Complete the mission within six minutes
Walkthrough:
- Follow the caravan until the cutscene. Roll the broken wheel back to the wagon and knock it into place.
- Drive the wagon to Horseshoe Overlook; the trip is quiet.
Tip: Javier waits just before the camp entrance, so stop the wagon next to him.

topics.title: Chapter 2: Horseshoe Overlook (overview)
topics.text:
The gang camps at Horseshoe Overlook, above Valentine.
- Missions: Polite Society, Valentine Style; Americans at Rest; Who is Not Without Sin; The First Shall Be Last; Paying a Social Call; Money Lending and Other Sins I-III; A Quiet Time; Exit Pursued by a Bruised Ego; Blessed are the Meek?; We Loved Once and True I-III; Good, Honest, Snake Oil; The Spines of America; Pouring Forth Oil I-IV; An American Pastoral Scene; A Fisher of Men; The Sheep and the Goats; A Strange Kindness.
- Activities that open up: poker, hunting with Charles, stables, home and shop robberies, table games, all challenge sets except Survivalist (that one opens with fishing after A Fisher of Men), special characters, and the shops (gunsmith, barber, general store, tailor, fence, doctor).
- Collectibles: cigarette cards, dinosaur bones and rock carvings.
- Strangers: Arcadia for Amateurs, American Dreams, The Smell of the Grease Paint, Fundraiser, A Fine Night For It, The Noblest of Men, and a Woman.
- Treasure hunts: Jack Hall Gang, High Stakes Treasure, and Le Trésor des Morts (pre-order bonus).
- Bounties: Ellie Anne Swan, Lindsey Wofford, later Joshua Brown. The Emerald Ranch wagon fence also becomes available.
- Weapons added to shops: Volcanic Pistol, Varmint Rifle, Springfield Rifle, Double-Barreled Shotgun, throwing knives, Pump-Action Shotgun, Rolling Block Rifle, Double-Action Revolver, Schofield Revolver, Lancaster Repeater.
- Ride at least 350 m from camp and come back to trigger a conversation with Ms Grimshaw.

topics.title: Polite Society, Valentine Style
topics.text:
Chapter 2. Talk to Uncle at the edge of camp and ride into Valentine.
Gold medal goals:
- Return the lost wagon horse to its owner
- Find Karen in under 45 seconds
Walkthrough:
- On the way you can help a coach driver by calming his runaway horse and leading it back (this is also the medal goal).
- In Valentine, follow Uncle and step in when a stranger assaults Tilly.
- In the hotel, go straight up to room 2B, kick the door in, knock out the man and follow Karen outside.
- When the man who recognizes you flees, borrow a horse and chase him, timing your gallop taps to save stamina. He ends up hanging from a cliff: saving him raises honor, letting him fall lowers it. Return the borrowed horse to its owner in Valentine for more honor.

topics.title: Americans at Rest
topics.text:
Chapter 2. Meet Javier and Charles in the Valentine saloon; a brawl breaks out.
Gold medal goals:
- Save Javier within 15 seconds
- Defeat Tommy within 1 minute 30 seconds
Walkthrough:
- Win your first fight, then help your three companions. Mash to break free from the man holding you, then rush to Javier, who's being beaten by Tommy, the giant from upstairs.
- Tommy can't be out-punched: block his swing, hit back once or twice, and repeat. Mash to escape his grabs.
New melee moves: block (then counter while the enemy is open), dodge (block with the right timing while aiming and tilting), and grapple, which lets you release, choke or punch the held enemy.

topics.title: Who is Not Without Sin
topics.text:
Chapter 2. Find Reverend Swanson at Flatneck Station, just southwest of camp.
Gold medal goals:
- Win two hands of poker
- Return Swanson to camp within 2 minutes 5 seconds
Walkthrough:
- Accept the poker invitation inside if you want a lesson (poker guide: page 220).
- Outside, find Swanson in the marked area (two people by the station give directions) and knock out his creditor; he's tough, so block first and then counter.
- A passer-by witnesses this: chase him and use Stop Witness, then threaten, beat, rob or fire a warning shot to keep him quiet. Otherwise you become wanted.
- Swanson gets his foot stuck at the nearby viaduct; free him quickly.
- Carry him to your horse, ride back, hitch at the marked spot and put him to bed.
Tip: sprint and gallop everywhere for the time goal.

topics.title: The First Shall Be Last
topics.text:
Chapter 2. Meet Javier just north of Blackwater to rescue Sean from bounty hunters.
Gold medal goals:
- Silently kill the bounty hunters by the river with Javier
- Shoot the rope to free Sean
- Get ten headshots
- Complete the mission without using any health items
Walkthrough:
- Blackwater is locked down and lawmen shoot on sight; stay by the river to the north to avoid them.
- Follow the boat down the river, scout with binoculars, then ride to the shore with your allies.
- Cross with Javier; after Trelawny's distraction, crouch up and knife the guard on the left.
- Push up the canyon cover to cover, taking out snipers with headshots. At the camp at the top, use the lock-on-and-flick technique for headshots.
- Shoot the rope Sean hangs from before the fight ends, then cut him free on the ground.

topics.title: Paying a Social Call
topics.text:
Chapter 2. Talk to Kieran (tied to a tree at camp) and ride with him and John to the Six Point Cabin O'Driscoll hideout.
Gold medal goals:
- Silently kill four O'Driscolls
- Get 12 headshots
- Finish with at least 80% accuracy
- Complete the mission without using any health items
Walkthrough:
- Bring the bow, Carbine Repeater and throwing knives from your horse.
- Take the lead to stay hidden. Knife the man relieving himself once his friends move off, then the next two (Bill kills one as you take the other), plus a lone guard at the foot of the hill. Lone guards show as red dots; bow headshots are the most reliable way to clear them.
- When only the campfire group is left, pick cover, open with a headshot and finish the fight, then head to the cabin.
- Search the cabin for money clips on the table and the Double-Barreled Shotgun above the chimney. Clean it with gun oil from the weapon wheel. There's more loot in the camp outside.

topics.title: Money Lending and Other Sins I & II
topics.text:
Chapter 2. Leopold Strauss, at the back of camp, sends you to collect from three debtors. One is enough to finish, but all three pays better. No medal goals.
- Mr Wrobel: small house in the marked area just west of camp. Confront him and loot the house; you can also take his horse from the barn.
- Chick Matthews: under a wooden canopy at Guthrie Farm, west of Emerald Ranch. Ask the man on the uprooted tree to point him out; Matthews rides off, so chase him (the lasso works well). He gives you a treasure map: go to the marked tree and check the hole in it.
- Lilly Millet: on a bench by a house at the north edge of Emerald Ranch, east of Valentine. Confronting her starts a fistfight with Cooper; block and counter, then loot him.
- Back at camp, use the tithing box beside Dutch's tent to unlock the ledger and buy your first camp upgrade (for example provisions, for better free food). Options: page 143.

topics.title: A Quiet Time
topics.text:
Chapter 2. Talk to Dutch in his tent, then ride to the Valentine saloon with Lenny and lean on the bar. The rest is best experienced unspoiled.
Gold medal goals:
- Try to make amends with an old rival
- Catch Lenny in the act
- Don't get arrested
Tips:
- When Lenny vanishes, he's first on the upstairs walkway, then on the bar, then in the main room.
- Tommy, the old rival, sits at a table in the main room during your first search for Lenny.
- The third time Lenny disappears, catch him in room 1A upstairs.
- To avoid arrest, run down the left side of the alley, dodge the wooden barrel, turn right and jump the fence. This leads to an alternative ending where you wake up in the wilderness.

topics.title: Exit Pursued by a Bruised Ego
topics.text:
Chapter 2. Hosea waits at camp to take you after a legendary bear.
Gold medal goals:
- Track the bear within 1 minute 30 seconds
- Shoot the bear at least six times
- Complete the mission within 12 minutes
Walkthrough:
- Move your saddle from your old horse to the new one (focus on the horse and hold to remove the saddle) and follow Hosea to Valentine.
- At the stable, decide what to do with the horse; you can buy a new one. A better horse is one of the best early investments.
- When Hosea asks for a rabbit, shoot one with the bow, set up camp from the item wheel, cook plain game twice and sleep till morning. This mission unlocks camping anywhere.
- Take your best weapons and use Eagle Eye to find clues. Inspect footprints, then follow the highlighted tracks to the next clue.
- Whether you use bait or split up, the bear attacks: fire during the automatic Dead Eye. Check on Hosea to finish.
Afterwards you can go back and hunt the bear properly as your first legendary animal (page 162).
Tip: the time goals are easy once you know where to go.

topics.title: Money Lending and Other Sins III
topics.text:
Chapter 2. Collect from Thomas Downes in the marked area just southwest of Valentine; he's a short walk east of the house.
Gold medal goals:
- Complete the mission within 2 minutes 10 seconds
Walkthrough: persuade him to pay however you choose, then report back to Strauss at camp.
Tip: beat him up to end the exchange fast, then hurry back.

topics.title: Blessed are the Meek?
topics.text:
Chapter 2. Break Micah out of the Strawberry jail. Arrive rested and well armed; there's a big shootout.
Gold medal goals:
- While escaping, kill all mounted lawmen within 55 seconds
- Get 15 headshots
- Finish with at least 70% accuracy
- Complete the mission without using any health items
Walkthrough:
- Talk to Micah through the barred window. Free him by hooking the steam donkey's cable to the cell window and pulling the lever, or use dynamite, or take the cell key from the lawmen inside.
- Fight through Strawberry's streets cover to cover, following Micah after each wave.
- Back at the jail, mount up and follow Micah, shooting pursuers off their horses, until you lose your wanted status.
Tip: a perfect place to practice the sharpshooter technique.

topics.title: The sharpshooter technique (instant headshots)
topics.text:
With the default aim assist, locking on puts your reticle on the target's chest.
- Hold aim to lock on.
- Give the right stick a tiny upward flick so the reticle sits on the head.
- Fire straight away for a headshot.
- Release aim and repeat on the next enemy.
With practice you can clear groups in seconds; special ammo helps too (page 284).

topics.title: We Loved Once and True I-III
topics.text:
Chapter 2. Read the letter on the table in Arthur's tent, then go to Mary's house at the north edge of Valentine. You can accept or refuse to help; refusing ends this story here.
Gold medal goals (Part III):
- Peacefully convince the Chelonians to let you take Jamie
- Return Jamie to Mary within two minutes
Walkthrough:
- Ride to the waypoint east of Cumberland Forest and walk to the Chelonians at the cliff edge.
- Choose the positive answer both times when talking to their leader.
- Chase Jamie when he bolts; it's a long ride, so time your gallop.
- At the train, half-press then fully press aim to trigger a brief Dead Eye and shoot the gun out of Jamie's hand (killing him fails the mission).
- Take him to Valentine station. Follow the railroad instead of the suggested route to save time; horse stimulants help you gallop the whole way.

topics.title: Good, Honest, Snake Oil
topics.text:
Chapter 2. Start at the Valentine sheriff's office: capture bounty Benedict Allbright, north of town, and bring him back.
Gold medal goals:
- Stop Benedict Allbright falling off the cliff
- Hogtie Allbright within 1 minute 15 seconds
- Return Allbright to the sheriff within 1 minute 30 seconds
Walkthrough:
- At the gorge, don't cross the river; take the cliff path beside it. When Allbright falls, pull him up by mashing.
- Gallop along the river after him, cross at the first chance, and lasso him in the shallow stretch where the current eases. Keep aiming as you dismount and hogtie him.
- Carry him back and drop him in the cell. Riding straight to the office instead of following the road saves seconds.

topics.title: The Spines of America
topics.text:
Chapter 2. Meet Hosea by the Emerald Ranch barn and ride northwest to rob the Carmody Dell house.
Gold medal goals:
- Loot all items from the Carmody Dell house
- Don't get spotted
- Deliver the wagon to Emerald Ranch within 1 minute 10 seconds
Walkthrough:
- Hitch your horse, hide behind the marked rock and watch the house through binoculars, then pick day or night.
- Night (easier): enter through the front while the owners sleep. Crouch the whole time, open doors gently, and close every door and drawer you open. Hosea waits on the stagecoach out front.
- Day: slip in the back while Hosea distracts at the front; you have a couple of minutes in an empty house. The chimney holds the main objective; there are three chests (two downstairs, one upstairs) plus furniture to search. Leave when Hosea starts saying goodbye, meet him in the barn, and turn left out of it to avoid witnesses.
- Drive the stagecoach back to Emerald Ranch.
Tip: the night version is the best route to gold. Take the food and drink too.

topics.title: Pouring Forth Oil I-IV
topics.text:
Chapter 2. John at camp asks you to steal an oil tank for a train robbery. This part is skipped if it's your only mission or if four in-game hours pass while it's active.
Gold medal goals (Part II):
- Deliver the wagon to the drop-off within 1 minute 45 seconds
Gold medal goals (Part IV):
- Kill all the train guards before Sean fires a shot
- Clear the baggage car of loot
- Escape the law within 1 minute 30 seconds
- Get ten kills using Dead Eye
- Complete the mission without using any health items
Walkthrough:
- Two tankers are marked: a hard one at Cornwall Kerosene & Tar, and an easier one driven from there to Valentine. For the easy one, kill the driver on the road (watch for witnesses) or take it once it's parked in Valentine.
- For the factory tank (just north of the railway, behind a fence with many guards), watch from the fence's northeast corner until the patrols leave the tank, climb over, and drive straight out, heading south out of the red circle.
- Take the tank to the drop-off, meet John at camp, then after an in-game hour meet him east of camp and head southwest.
- Park across the tracks, then rob passengers in both carriages with John.
- At the baggage car, Dead Eye the man attacking Sean, then the one on the roof above, then two more inside. Search the chest and cabinets at the far end.
- Hold the train against two waves of lawmen, then gallop due north out of the search area.
Tip: the factory tank is much closer to the drop-off, which makes the Part II goal easy. Tag several heads in Dead Eye to save Sean.

topics.title: An American Pastoral Scene
topics.text:
Chapter 2. Find Micah at a campfire overlooking the forest just east of Strawberry and wait for the stagecoach.
Gold medal goals:
- Headshot each of the mounted guards protecting the wagon
- Kill ten enemies using Dead Eye
- Complete the mission within 5 minutes 50 seconds
- Complete the mission without using any health items
Walkthrough:
- The escort riders are bunched together: tag all their heads in Dead Eye and fire. Refill Dead Eye with a tonic if needed. Galloping close makes the headshots easier.
- Climb onto the stagecoach; when you're ambushed, pick off the attackers with your new weapon from cover.
- Rejoin Micah at the coach and shoot the lock.

topics.title: A Fisher of Men
topics.text:
Chapter 2. Speak to Abigail in her tent and then Jack, and ride to the marked riverbank. Unlocks fishing and the Survivalist challenges.
Gold medal goals:
- After arriving at the river, catch a fish within 1 minute 30 seconds
- Complete the mission within 7 minutes 20 seconds
Walkthrough:
- Equip the rod from the item wheel and cheese from the bait wheel, cast like firing a weapon, and strike when you feel a bite.
- Tilt against the fish as it pulls and reel clockwise when it tires; repeat until it's landed. Re-bait (quick-equip cheese) for the second fish.
- Ride back to camp after the cutscene.
Tip: both goals are easy even first time.

topics.title: The Sheep and the Goats
topics.text:
Chapter 2's finale. Meet John at the Valentine auction yard.
Gold medal goals:
- Herd all the sheep back to the pen in Valentine
- Get 35 headshots
- Finish with at least 80% accuracy
- Complete the mission without using any health items
Walkthrough:
- Buy the Rolling Block Rifle from the Valentine gunsmith (Rifles section of his catalogue).
- Follow John to a ridge and fire near the ranchers to scare them off without hitting them; look for the big flock to spot them.
- Herd the sheep to Valentine's auction yard: ride behind them, round up stragglers fast and don't trample any. Shouting or shooting nearby speeds them up.
- In the saloon, half-press then fully press to trigger Dead Eye and tag the two men holding your friends first.
- Fight down the street protecting Strauss from behind the cart; enemies hide in windows, on balconies and on the stable roof.
- At the end of the street, put Strauss on John's horse, then break away and gallop south (following the railroad works) until you lose the law.
Tip: use Dead Eye freely; tonics like snake oil that refill and fortify Dead Eye help a lot.

topics.title: A Strange Kindness
topics.text:
Chapter 2. Talk to Dutch in his tent and ride with Charles to Dewberry Creek in the southeast.
Gold medal goals:
- Return the captive to his family within 1 minute 40 seconds
- Get five headshots
- Finish with at least 80% accuracy
- Complete the mission without using any health items
Walkthrough:
- Search the marked area, then the camp nearby: check both tents and behind the crates.
- Ride south to the lakeside camp and free the settler lying on the ground. When the ambush starts, open with Dead Eye for three quick headshots, then get two more.
- Cut him free and carry him home to Dewberry Creek.

topics.title: Chapter 3: Clemens Point (overview)
topics.text:
Run out of Valentine by Cornwall and wary of Pinkertons watching the westward routes, the gang moves southeast to Clemens Point near Rhodes.
- Missions: The New South; Further Questions of Female Suffrage; American Distillation; The Course of True Love I-III; Advertising, the New American Art I & II; Horse Flesh for Dinner; The Fine Joys of Tobacco; Magicians for Sport; Friends in Very Low Places; An Honest Mistake; Preaching Forgiveness as He Went; Sodom? Back to Gomorrah; Blessed are the Peacemakers; A Short Walk in a Pretty Town; Blood Feuds, Ancient and Modern; The Battle of Shady Belle. An American Pastoral Scene can be done in Chapter 2 or 3.
- Strangers: No Good Deed (opens after two more missions following American Distillation), He's British, of Course (disabled for four in-game hours after American Distillation), Money Lending and Other Sins IV (unavailable after A Short Walk in a Pretty Town), The Iniquities of History.
- Activities: home robbery with Sean, fishing with Kieran and with Javier, coach robberies, and the horse fence.
- Legendary fish become available (page 164).
- Loansharking: Gwyn Hughes, Winton Holmes.
- Weapons: fire bottles, Bolt Action Rifle.

topics.title: The New South
topics.text:
Chapter 3. Walk to Dutch at the shore and follow him and Hosea until you meet Trelawny.
Gold medal goals:
- Catch and return Anders Anderson to jail within 5 minutes 30 seconds
- Knock out Anders Anderson without taking a hit
- Catch a fish with Dutch and Hosea
Walkthrough:
- Gallop after the train. The Anderson boys must be taken alive, so keep weapons holstered, and you only have a few minutes before the train leaves the sheriff's jurisdiction.
- Jump onto the car with the wooden crates and mash to shake off the man who grabs you.
- Beat one brother in a rooftop fistfight (block, then counter) and the other in the last car. Load him on your horse and follow Archibald to Rhodes; drop him outside the sheriff's office.
- Accept Hosea's fishing invitation to continue (refusing ends the mission): row the boat by tapping in time with the oars, equip the lake lure, cast, reel slowly to attract fish, strike on a bite, and fight the fish until it tires.
- Put the rod away and row back to camp.

topics.title: Further Questions of Female Suffrage
topics.text:
Chapter 3. Start with Pearson at camp, then drive the wagon to the Rhodes general store with Sadie.
Gold medal goals:
- Fend off the Lemoyne Raiders in less than one minute
- Get five headshots
- Finish with at least 85% accuracy
- Complete the mission without consuming any health items
Walkthrough:
- After you split from Sadie, send your letter at the marked post office booth, then get back on the wagon.
- Stay alert on the ride. When Sadie pulls over and opens fire, shoot the mounted Raiders with quick headshots, then take cover and clear the rest (follow the red radar dots). Keep Sadie alive.
- Drive back to camp with her.
Tip: trigger Dead Eye early with several Raiders in view and sprint toward the stragglers.

topics.title: American Distillation
topics.text:
Chapter 3. Begins at the Rhodes sheriff's office; get on the wagon outside.
Gold medal goals:
- Win the race back to camp
- Get 10 headshots
- Complete the mission without taking any damage
- Finish with at least 70% accuracy
Walkthrough:
- At the crime scene, follow Archibald, then drive to the swamp.
- Knock out the moonshiners unseen with no weapons. Right path: creep through the bushes to the two talking guards and stun the one left by the tree, then optionally ambush the second from behind the vine-covered trees. Left path: use the big trees as cover, take out the man by the cart, cross the bridge and get the second from behind. Hogtie and carry them to the wagon.
- Plant dynamite in the marked spot, light it and back off to blow the still.
- Join Bill in a big fight with the Lemoyne Raiders; go slowly from cover, and watch for enemies inside cabins.
- Optionally race Dutch back to camp: gallop in rhythm, cut corners, and ease off near the end to avoid hitting a tree just before camp.

topics.title: The Course of True Love I & II
topics.text:
Chapter 3. Go to Caliga Hall east of Rhodes, talk to a guard at the entrance, then to Beau Gray outside the wood store, and head to the edge of Braithwaite Manor southwest of Rhodes.
Gold medal goals:
- Reach Penelope without getting spotted
- Finish within three minutes
Walkthrough:
- Guards show as red dots. Swing wide around the south of the property and swim through the small cove to the gazebo where Penelope waits.
- To leave unseen, go back through the cove and straight south, or steal the boat across from the gazebo stairs and row west out of the red zone.

topics.title: The Course of True Love III
topics.text:
Chapter 3. Meet Beau Gray in the Caliga Hall stable and follow him to Rhodes.
Gold medal goals:
- Finish within 4 minutes 15 seconds
Walkthrough:
- After the cutscene, go to the side alley to face Beau's cousins: defuse to avoid violence, or antagonize for a brawl (block and counter).
- Then mount up and follow Beau.
Tip: for the fastest time, ignore the cousins and leave with Beau right away.

topics.title: Advertising, the New American Art I & II
topics.text:
Chapter 3. Speak to Abigail at camp; a marker appears to the northeast where Hosea and John wait by a wagon.
Gold medal goals:
- Headshot five Lemoyne Raiders in the saloon
- Finish with at least 90% accuracy
- Complete the mission without consuming any health items
Walkthrough:
- Drive the wagon to the front door of Braithwaite Manor to the south, then back to Rhodes, parking outside the saloon.
- Carry moonshine from the wagon to behind the bar and follow the prompts until the Raiders burst in.
- From behind the bar you can headshot three or four in one Dead Eye.
- When Hosea calls, clear the ground floor, vault the bar, run upstairs and headshot the man threatening him (a short Dead Eye helps). Kill the two on the balcony and jump down to the wagon.
- With no cover on the escape, shoot pursuers behind the wagon quickly; snake oil refills Dead Eye.
Tip: the accuracy goal is strict, so aim carefully and lean on Dead Eye.

topics.title: Horse Flesh for Dinner
topics.text:
Chapter 3. Go to the entrance of Caliga Hall, meet John and Javier at the Gray stables, and ride to the Braithwaite stables.
Gold medal goals:
- Kill the stablehand showing you the horses
- Catch the stallion within 10 seconds
- Get five headshots
Walkthrough:
- Inside, stealth-kill the stablehand from behind, put on your bandana, calm the white horse and lead it out.
- On the escape, stay close to Javier and drop pursuers with the sharpshooter technique (page 47).
- When a stallion bolts, chase it and lasso it, keeping aim held until it's caught, then ride on with Javier to the rustlers.
Tip: have the lasso ready and throw it the moment the stallion breaks away.

topics.title: The Fine Joys of Tobacco
topics.text:
Chapter 3. Starts as you enter Braithwaite Manor. Drive the wagon to Caliga Hall with Sean and hide in the back when prompted.
Gold medal goals:
- Silently kill the Gray when Sean distracts him in the wagon store
- Douse the fields within 2 minutes 20 seconds
- Kill five Grays during the escape
- Complete the mission without consuming any health items
Walkthrough:
- In the wagon store, sneak out and quietly kill Hamish from behind.
- Hide behind the barrels, then crouch through the highlighted tobacco fields, holding fire to pour moonshine until each marking disappears. Only cross guarded paths when sentries are far away or facing elsewhere. Tapping the radar button zooms it out for a wider view, and holding it lets you make that permanent.
- Meet Sean at the barn, throw a fire bottle in, then torch the marked fields.
- Fight the guards cover to cover near Sean (Dead Eye on groups), cut the horses free at the wagon and escape.
Tip: keep moving from field to field without stopping; the escape doesn't need rushing.

topics.title: Magicians for Sport
topics.text:
Chapter 3. Speak to Dutch in his tent, then Charles, and ride to Trelawny's marked location.
Gold medal goals:
- Inspect all the clues in Trelawny's caravan
- While tracking, stay within 30 feet of Trelawny's trail
- Kill two bounty hunters in the cornfields within one minute
- Complete the mission without consuming any health items
Walkthrough:
- Caravan clues (Eagle Eye highlights them): the food on the table, the unmade bed, and the bloody towel on the bathtub.
- Follow the tracks to a small camp by the forest, win the fistfight (block, counter) and interrogate the man Charles holds. Killing or releasing him changes your honor.
- Follow Charles to the cabin. Three bounty hunters hide in the cornfields: one to your left, one to your right, and the third, who can only be caught last, in the far field on the right. Watch for disturbances like birds taking off; Charles also points you to them.
- In the shootout by the barn, kill the man at the entrance and the sniper in the opening above quickly, or the sniper retreats inside.
The sniper drops the rare rolling block rifle, a unique weapon needed for the compendium.
Tip: sprint to the first two hunters and tackle them, then finish them on the ground.

topics.title: Friends in Very Low Places
topics.text:
Chapter 3. Speak to Trelawny, leaning on a tree at the edge of camp, and ride with him to the Rhodes post office.
Gold medal goals:
- Complete the mission without being spotted
- Complete the mission within 8 minutes 10 seconds
Walkthrough:
- Go inside with Trelawny; after paying Alden, ride with him to Hill Haven Ranch.
- Tail the stagecoach at a distance. When it stops, dismount and crouch to the bushes by the road sign, and go no farther.
- When Mrs. Damsen starts singing, sneak to the back of the coach, break the lockbox and take its contents, then crouch back to the same bushes.
- Once the coach leaves, rejoin Trelawny.

topics.title: An Honest Mistake
topics.text:
Chapter 3. Speak to Molly at camp, then ride with Uncle to the crossroads and put on your bandana when prompted.
Gold medal goals:
- Save Uncle when he is overpowered
- Get 20 headshots
- Finish with at least 80% accuracy
- Complete the mission without consuming any health items
Walkthrough:
- Search the crate at the back of the wagon when it arrives.
- A large fight breaks out at the old barn, with reinforcements. Shoot from cover and switch sides using your companions' calls and the red threat markers.
- Leaving the barn, follow Uncle into the woods, hide behind a rock, take down the two passing guards from behind, and help Uncle with his.
- Help Charles and Bill by shooting attackers from behind the trees.
- On the gallop away, a full Dead Eye can take out five or six bunched riders. Otherwise wait for open ground, swing the camera back and focus on aiming.
Tip: it's all execution; the sharpshooter technique (page 47) is key.

topics.title: Preaching Forgiveness as He Went
topics.text:
Chapter 3. Speak to Lenny at the south edge of camp and follow him.
Gold medal goals:
- Kill 10 Lemoyne Raiders with a long scoped rifle
- Finish within 11 minutes 30 seconds
- Finish with at least 70% accuracy
- Complete the mission without consuming any health items
Walkthrough:
- At the abandoned church, tail the wagon at a distance to the Shady Belle mansion and dismount in the marked area. Bring your Rolling Block Rifle.
- Take cover behind the wall across from Lenny and scope out the red dynamite crates. Open by shooting the dynamite, or send Lenny in as a distraction (he's a bit more effective that way).
- Snipe from the wall, which gives cover and a good view; still targets are easiest. Lenny eventually wins his wrestling match without help. When a Raider mans the Gatling gun on the balcony above the front door, kill him at once by aiming just above the barrel.
- Leaving, three more Raiders confront you and it turns into a shootout either way: strike first or Dead Eye all three. Drive back to camp.

topics.title: Sodom? Back to Gomorrah
topics.text:
Chapter 3. Speak to Bill in the wagon at the edge of camp and follow him to Valentine to rob the bank.
Gold medal goals:
- Loot all the safes
- Headshot five mounted lawmen during the horseback escape
- Get to the Downes ranch within 1 minute 55 seconds
- Finish with at least 70% accuracy
- Complete the mission without consuming any health items
Walkthrough:
- Pick either distraction for Karen (both work the same). Inside, open the teller's door and make him open the vault.
- Crack the five safes or blow them. Cracking takes longer, but done within six minutes it avoids the big fight outside. Turn the dial counterclockwise, clockwise, then counterclockwise, slowing when the vibration strengthens until it clicks; if you overshoot, keep turning the same way back to the spot.
- Safe combinations, left to right: 34-69-22, 16-40-55, 37-1-69, 15-7-55, 68-12-38.
- Dynamite route: prime all five safes, light one fuse, hide in the other room, collect the money, then fight down the street (opening Dead Eye for up to three lawmen, cover behind the cart on the right, a gunman on the balcony). You can run for your horse at the end.
- Escape with the gang, shooting back on straight stretches, and ride to Downes Ranch once the group splits.
Tip: snake oil's fortified Dead Eye makes headshots on moving riders much easier.

topics.title: Blessed are the Peacemakers
topics.text:
Chapter 3. Talk to Micah in Dutch's tent and ride with them to the lookout spot. Watch Dutch and Micah through binoculars or the Rolling Block Rifle's scope.
Gold medal goals:
- Free yourself and perform self-surgery within one minute
- Recover your weapons from the O'Driscoll camp
- Kill the O'Driscoll gang members that beat and shot you
- Escape the O'Driscoll camp without being spotted
Walkthrough:
- Captured, swing on your shackles (tilt side to side) to reach the metal file on the table, grab it, cauterize the wound as prompted, and stealth-kill the O'Driscoll who comes in.
- Outside, you can kill all nearby guards with throwing knives, but only the man checking the crate by the shed must die. Get your weapons by the shed door (gun icon on the radar), take your horse by the campfire and leave by the east path.
- Ride back to camp avoiding the patrols shown as red dots.
Tip: the two who beat and shot you guard the cabin. Use the throwing knives from the basement: turn left at the top of the stairs to kill the man studying the wall, then go back for the one near your weapons.

topics.title: A Short Walk in a Pretty Town
topics.text:
Chapter 3. Meet Bill, Micah and Sean outside the Rhodes bank.
Gold medal goals:
- Kill three lawmen in Dead Eye while saving Bill
- Get 20 headshots
- Complete the mission using sidearms only
- Finish within 4 minutes 30 seconds
- Complete the mission without consuming any health items
Walkthrough:
- After the cutscene, hold your first cover and pick off foes, prioritizing the rooftop ahead and the balcony to the left. When enemies come from behind, move to the cart.
- When Micah moves, go to the back of the marked gun store; an enemy jumps out on your left, and there's a Double-Barreled Shotgun to grab. Kick the locked door, pre-aim at the man at the end of the corridor, then two more around the corner. Shoot street gunmen from under the window.
- Follow Micah and drop the hostage-takers in the automatic Dead Eye.
Tip: dual-wield sidearms for more ammo and flexibility, and use the sharpshooter technique throughout.

topics.title: Blood Feuds, Ancient and Modern
topics.text:
Chapter 3. Starts automatically near Dutch's tent; ride with the gang to Braithwaite Manor.
Gold medal goals:
- Headshot Gareth and Gerald Braithwaite
- Get 20 headshots
- Finish with at least 85% accuracy
- Complete the mission without consuming any health items
Walkthrough:
- After the cutscene, take cover and fire on the attackers, balconies first.
- Search the manor for Jack and shoot the man who springs up from behind the overturned desk.
- Join Dutch upstairs and use a balcony pillar as cover against reinforcements at the front gate; Dead Eye them while they're bunched. A second wave comes on the east side: same tactic.
- Help John break the door, then tag Gareth's and Gerald's heads in the automatic Dead Eye. Two headshots are enough; don't empty your gun into them. Leave with Dutch.

topics.title: The Battle of Shady Belle
topics.text:
Ride with John to take Shady Belle from the Lemoyne Raiders; it becomes the gang's next camp.
Gold medal goals:
- Kill all the Lemoyne Raiders in Shady Belle
- Clear two bodies from Shady Belle within 1 minute 40 seconds
- Finish within 11 minutes
Walkthrough:
- Deal with the two men who greet you, then clear the house: one inside on the ground floor and three upstairs, each in a different room. Meet John at the entrance.
- Carry the marked body to the swamp by the jetty and dump it; repeat once more.
- Follow Dutch to Saint Denis.
Tip: ride in a straight line across the plains and forests, use Dead Eye so John doesn't steal your kills at the start, and dump the bodies quickly.

topics.title: Chapter 4: Shady Belle (overview)
topics.text:
After the Gray-Braithwaite feud ends in disaster (Sean dead, Jack kidnapped, Pinkertons back on their trail), the gang moves to Shady Belle near Saint Denis, where Jack is being held.
- Missions: The Joys of Civilization; Angelo Bronte, a Man of Honor; Help a Brother Out; Brothers and Sisters, One and All; Fatherhood and Other Dreams; No, No and Thrice, No; The Gilded Cage; A Fine Night of Debauchery; Horsemen, Apocalypses; Urban Pleasures; Country Pursuits; Revenge is a Dish Best Eaten; American Fathers I & II (two in-game hours apart); Banking, the Old American Art.
- Time-sensitive: Brothers and Sisters, One and All and Fatherhood and Other Dreams must be done in Chapter 4.
- Strangers: The Ties that Bind Us, A Bright Bouncing Boy, The Artist's Way, The Mercies of Knowledge, Money Lending and Other Sins V, Idealism and Pragmatism for Beginners, Oh, Brother, and The Noblest of Men, and a Woman III & IV.
- Bounties: Mark Johnson, Robbie Laidlaw. Loansharking: Algie Davison, plus Winton Holmes and Gwyneth Hughes if Money Lending IV isn't done.
- Activities: coach robberies with Micah and Lenny, bank robbery with Charles (Special/Ultimate Edition only), hunting with Pearson, rustling with Uncle.
- Collectibles: Exotics for Algernon (page 206).
- Weapons: Semi-Automatic Pistol, Semi-Auto Shotgun.

topics.title: The Joys of Civilization
topics.text:
Chapter 4. Meet Dutch outside the Bastille Saloon in the westernmost highlighted area of Saint Denis and call the bartender over.
Gold medal goals:
- Catch the street urchin before he reaches the market
- Finish within 5 minutes 30 seconds
Walkthrough:
- In the alley nearby, the children you want are just past the metal archway on the east side of the search area. Follow them and give chase after the cutscene; you can steal a horse.
- When the kid gets off the trolley, search the highlighted area; the men chatting by the fountain say he's just beyond the round archway.
- Climb over the barred door (or kick it open) and up the railing when he takes to the rooftops.
- At the market, ask around to expose the thief, chase him once more, then find Dutch on a bench outside the park near the saloon.
Tip: after the trolley, run straight through the round archway without talking to anyone and tackle him as soon as you see him.

topics.title: Angelo Bronte, a Man of Honor
topics.text:
Chapter 4. Meet Dutch and John on the steps of Bronte's mansion, then follow John to the cemetery.
Gold medal goals:
- Encounter the dog and the drunk
- Don't get spotted by the law
- Finish within 11 minutes
- Get four headshots
Walkthrough:
- Go to the far northeast corner and inspect the mausoleum to find the grave robbers, then hunt them from behind gravestones.
- On the east side, search the mausoleum with the metal fence gate for the stash.
- When lawmen arrive, stay close to John and use the radar to reach the exit unseen.
- Ride back to Bronte's, then to camp.
Tip: the easy goal to miss: before heading to the mausoleum, interact with the dog near the south entrance and the drunk by a grave just north of the central dome.

topics.title: Help a Brother Out
topics.text:
Chapter 4. Go to the stranger marker on the east side of Saint Denis to meet Brother Dorkins. Donating to the poor in the cutscene gives a little honor.
Gold medal goals:
- Find the captives without threatening the shop owner
- Finish within 2 minutes 45 seconds
Walkthrough:
- Enter the shop through the green door. You could threaten the owner into revealing the trick (pull a book), but for the medal use Eagle Eye to spot the scratches on the floor of the room opposite his counter and force the bookcase yourself.
- Free the two captives in the basement and return to Brother Dorkins.

topics.title: Brothers and Sisters, One and All
topics.text:
Chapter 4 (time-sensitive: last chance in Chapter 4). One in-game hour after Help a Brother Out, Brother Dorkins is on the steps of a church in north Saint Denis.
Gold medal goals:
- Find the kid within 19 seconds
Walkthrough:
- Sprint south to the marked area and talk to the man who was knocked over; this reveals a second area. Confront the man restraining the kid and pick up the crucifix.
- Find Sister Calderon without alerting the law. Coming in from the street to the northeast, you can walk casually behind the guard at the telegraph post to reach her by the church steps.
- After the cutscene, sprint northwest out of the red circle, hide in a back alley and wait for the wanted meter to empty.
Tip: just sprint straight to the kid.

topics.title: Fatherhood and Other Dreams
topics.text:
Chapter 4 (time-sensitive: last chance in Chapter 4). Read the letter in Arthur's room, then meet Mary at the Grand Hotel in Saint Denis. It's optional; if you refuse, you won't get another chance.
Gold medal goals:
- Catch the wagon and take it to the secluded spot within 1 minute 45 seconds
- Take Mary to the theater
Walkthrough:
- Ride to the stables to the southwest, then tail Mary's father at a distance; Mary's comments keep you on track.
- Chase the buyer's fast wagon out of Saint Denis, jump aboard from the side, clear the two men from the driver's seat and drive to the marked secluded spot.
- Pull the buyer down. He asks $100 for Mary's brooch; beating him drops it to $50, then $25, and one more time makes him hand it over free.
- Return to Mary and accept her invitation to the theater.
Tip: gallop in rhythm to catch the wagon fast.

topics.title: No, No and Thrice, No
topics.text:
Chapter 4. Speak to Mary-Beth at camp and drive northwest to Radley's House with Ms Grimshaw (you can let her handle the lone guard).
Gold medal goals:
- Kill both of the Foreman boys yourself during the chase
- Finish with at least 90% accuracy
Walkthrough:
- Storm the house: one man in the kitchen, one in the bedroom where Tilly is tied up. Cut her free.
- In the horse chase, gallop close and headshot the first two riders. Anthony Foreman must be taken alive: lasso him, hogtie him and bring him to Tilly.
Tip: Ms Grimshaw opens fire once you're close, so use Dead Eye for long-range headshots before she gets the kills.

topics.title: The Gilded Cage
topics.text:
Chapter 4. Find Hosea by the gazebo at camp and follow the prompts until the fireworks. The mayor stands by the fountain.
Gold medal goals:
- While at the party, pour some drinks, compliment a guest's attire, accept a gift and save a life
- Follow the servant without being detected
The four party tasks:
- Offer champagne to the thirsty ladies near the dome.
- Compliment the lady in front of the dome on her headdress.
- Accept a ticket from the two men discussing theater between the dome and the fountain.
- Help Algernon Wasp at the small buffet table near the canopy when he starts choking.
Walkthrough:
- Tail the servant from a distance; the three times he stops to talk inside, stay back out of sight. There's no rush.
- When he goes upstairs into an office and moves to the next room, take the document from the ledger on the marked desk, then leave the gala with Dutch.

topics.title: A Fine Night of Debauchery
topics.text:
Chapter 4. Meet Trelawny in north Saint Denis.
Gold medal goals:
- Win the game of poker without Strauss's help
- After your cover is blown, escape the boat in under 35 seconds
- Get five headshots
- Complete the mission without consuming any health items
Walkthrough:
- Buy the designated suit at the tailor's, get a cut at the barber's, then take the carriage to the riverboat, the Grand Korrigan.
- At the poker table (guide on page 220) the dealer is on your side: fold the first game, which you'd lose anyway, then feel free to go all-in.
- When your opponent is bust, follow the pit boss to the safe room, disarm him, shoot during the automatic Dead Eye as you go for the safe, then finish the theft and follow Javier to the bar.
- In the shootout, stay behind the counter landing headshots. When Javier heads for the exit, sprint through the door and corridor and jump into the water.
Tip: kill quickly and stand near the exit so you can dash out the moment it opens.

topics.title: Horsemen, Apocalypses
topics.text:
Chapter 4. Greet Sadie by the front door of the house at camp; O'Driscolls attack Shady Belle.
Gold medal goals:
- Shoot the O'Driscolls in the boat before they disembark
- Get 15 headshots
- Finish with at least 70% accuracy
- Complete the mission while exclusively using sidearms
- Complete the mission without consuming any health items
Walkthrough:
- From the balcony, pick off as many as you can, stationary ones first. Go down to the front door when Dutch asks, then retreat inside when John says so and push the cabinet over to barricade the door.
- Defend the back windows (Arthur breaks the glass when you aim from cover beside one). When Sadie screams, jump out of the window and run to her behind the nearby cabin.
- Push on with Sadie to the cover ahead; two O'Driscolls arrive by boat. Finish the fight toward the mansion entrance, staying close to her.
Tip: for the boat goal, sprint to the crate a few steps past Sadie's cover and shoot the two boatmen before they land.

topics.title: Urban Pleasures
topics.text:
Chapter 4. Find Dutch in a back alley in southeast Saint Denis.
Gold medal goals:
- Rob all the customers in the trolley station
- Kill 10 lawmen while on the trolley
- Prevent any lawmen from jumping on the back of the wagon
- Shoot the dynamite thrown by Lenny
- Complete the mission without consuming any health items
Walkthrough:
- When it starts, hold up and rob each customer, then make the cashier open the safe.
- On the trolley, track red dots and switch sides to kill as many lawmen as possible.
- In the wagon escape, kill the closest pursuers first so none jump on the back.
- Approaching the bridge roadblock, headshot a couple of lawmen at range, then shoot Lenny's dynamite in midair during the automatic Dead Eye.
- After the crash, hold out until Lenny and Dutch find a way, then follow them through the archway, courtyard and street, cover to cover, to a wagon.
Tip: short Dead Eye bursts for single headshots on riders; use Dead Eye tonics freely.

topics.title: Country Pursuits
topics.text:
Chapter 4. Meet Dutch on the balcony above the house's front door at camp and ride with him.
Gold medal goals:
- Return Jules to the skiff within 1 minute 40 seconds
- Shoot the bullgator five times
Walkthrough:
- In Lagras, help Thomas with his traps. After the second one, wait for the three alligators to swim past as he warns.
- When the group splits, go to the marked area ahead, call Jules down from his tree branch and head to the skiff.
- Shoot at the bullgator; its foam shows where it is, and a red reticle means you'll hit. Treat Jules's wounds as prompted, then drive it off again when it returns.
- When the skiff hits a stump, jump into the water, find Jules in the marked zone, and sprint straight back to the skiff with him.
Tip: run in straight lines both ways for the time goal; a fortified stamina meter helps.

topics.title: Revenge is a Dish Best Eaten
topics.text:
Chapter 4. Meet Dutch on the pier outside Thomas's cabin in Lagras.
Gold medal goals:
- Search every room in Bronte's mansion
- Get Bronte to the skiff within 1 minute 30 seconds
- Get 20 headshots
- Complete the mission without consuming any health items
Walkthrough:
- Climb into Bronte's grounds, follow John, take cover behind the fountain and open with a headshot. Push past it as reinforcements arrive; shoot the balcony gunmen first, since they can hit you behind cover.
- Inside, clear Bronte's men from behind walls, then go upstairs.
- Search all three highlighted rooms. Bronte is in the middle one, straight ahead at the top of the stairs. Pick him up and head down as the lawmen arrive.
- Carrying Bronte means no cover, so hang back and let the others thin the enemies, or rely on quick headshots, until you reach the skiff.
Tip: search the other two rooms before grabbing Bronte.

topics.title: American Fathers I & II
topics.text:
Chapter 4. Speak to Evelyn Miller in Saint Denis. Two in-game hours later, an Eagle Flies marker appears southeast of Valentine.
Gold medal goals:
- Infiltrate the factory by hiding in the wagon
- Reach Danbury's office without being detected
- Kill all the horseback pursuers during the escape
- Finish with at least 80% accuracy
Walkthrough:
- Wagon route (easier, and a medal goal): sprint downhill, hide in the wagon, hop out when it stops, climb the stairs and go through the door into the factory.
- On-foot route: come in from the southwest corner along the railway, wait for the platform guard to leave (or arrow him), then sneak into the main room.
- From the wagon entry, wait for the nearest guard to step out through the big opening on the left, then crouch along that side to the stairs at the back, using the machines as cover. From the on-foot entry, go through the opening and turn left for the stairs.
- Upstairs, one guard watches the window: sneak past or take him down quietly. In the end office, beat Danbury for the file and leave through the window.
- Fight to the explosion site, find Eagle Flies in the marked area, and ride with him, shooting pursuers by turning the camera back without slowing down.

topics.title: Banking, the Old American Art
topics.text:
Chapter 4's finale. Speak to Dutch inside the mansion at camp and follow the convoy to Saint Denis. Set your loadout before leaving your horse.
Gold medal goals:
- Crack the safe without making a mistake
- Complete the mission with sidearms exclusively
- Get 25 headshots
- Complete the mission without consuming any health items
Walkthrough:
- Force the manager to open the vault, then crack the safe (counterclockwise, clockwise, counterclockwise, going slowly when the vibration strengthens until it clicks). Safe combination: 19-72-54.
- In the shootout, hold your first cover; when Dutch calls, join him behind the counter, plant his dropped dynamite on the marked wall, take cover and shoot it.
- Go through the hole, up the ladder to the marked rooftop spot, and snipe enemies below while the gang climbs; balconies first. Kill the Gatling gunner on the wagon by aiming just above the muzzle flash.
- Cross the rooftops with the gang to a window, then follow Dutch to the docks.
- In the train car, crouch and duck behind the seats on the left when the lantern guard appears. Outside, whistle from the marked spot to draw guards off, slip around the crates, and after Charles's diversion run to the boat.
Tip: put away the rifle Javier hands you at the hole in the wall to keep the sidearms-only goal.

topics.title: Chapter 5: Guarma (overview)
topics.text:
After the failed Saint Denis bank job, the gang stows away on a southbound ship and is shipwrecked on Guarma.
- Guarma missions: Welcome to the New World, Savagery Unleashed, A Kind and Benevolent Despot, Hell Hath No Fury, Paradise Mercifully Departed.
- Back on the mainland: Dear Uncle Tacitus, Fleeting Joy, That's Murfree Country, which leads into Chapter 6. Icarus and Friends (and A Fork in the Road, which triggers just before it) can be done in Chapter 5 or 6.
- Last chance to finish Good, Honest, Snake Oil before That's Murfree Country. Bounty hunting is locked after That's Murfree Country.
- Strangers: The Wisdom of the Elders (after Fleeting Joy), The Veteran (after That's Murfree Country).
